'''Michael Paul Snyder''' is an American [[Genomics|genomicist]], professor, and former chair of [[genetics]] at [[Stanford University School of Medicine]]. He also serves as the director of the Stanford Center for Genomics and Personalized Medicine.<ref name=StanfordEdu>{{cite web |url=https://profiles.stanford.edu/michael-snyder |title=Michael Snyder, Ph.D., STANFORD W. ASCHERMAN PROFESSOR OF GENETICS |last= |first= |date=20 August 2015 |website= Stanford profiles|access-date=19 April 2022}}</ref><ref name="auto7">{{Cite web|url=https://genestogenomes.org/snyder-beadle/|title=Congratulations to Michael Snyder for receiving the 2019 George W. Beadle Award!|date=2 April 2019|accessdate=16 May 2022}}</ref> 

Snyder's research focuses on "[[omics]]", the study of genomes, transcriptomes, proteomes, and other high-throughput omics datasets. His lab has contributed to understanding the genomes and transcriptomes of yeast and humans. The lab also pioneered the use of multi-omic longitudinal profiling to monitor health.<ref>{{cite journal |vauthors=Zhou W, Sailani MR, Contrepois K, Zhou Y, Ahadi S, Leopold SR, Zhang MJ, Rao V, Avina M, Mishra T, Johnson J, Lee-McMullen B, Chen S, Metwally AA, Tran TD, Nguyen H, Zhou X, Albright B, Hong BY, Petersen L, Bautista E, Hanson B, Chen L, Spakowicz D, Bahmani A, Salins D, Leopold B, Ashland M, Dagan-Rosenfeld O, Rego S, Limcaoco P, Colbert E, Allister C, Perelman D, Craig C, Wei E, Chaib H, Hornburg D, Dunn J, Liang L, Rose SM, Kukurba K, Piening B, Rost H, Tse D, McLaughlin T, Sodergren E, Weinstock GM, Snyder M|display-authors=6 |title=Longitudinal multi-omics of host-microbe dynamics in prediabetes |journal=Nature |volume=569 |issue=7758 |pages=663–71 |date=May 2019 |pmid=31142858 |pmc=6666404 |doi=10.1038/s41586-019-1236-x |bibcode=2019Natur.569..663Z |url=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.thermofisher.com/us/en/home/global/forms/industrial/multi-omics-redefine-precision-health.html|title = How Multi-Omics Profiling Can Redefine Precision Health and Medicine - US|website=ThermoFisher Scientific}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Snyder was born in 1955 and grew up outside of [[Pottstown, Pennsylvania]].<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://ctcase.org/member/michael-p-snyder/|title=Michael P. Snyder|accessdate=16 May 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Marcus |first=Amy Dockser |date=14 May 2012 |title=What Happens When One Man's Genome Is Revealed |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/BL-HEB-49289 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220420041348/https://www.wsj.com/articles/BL-HEB-49289 |archive-date=2022-04-20 |accessdate=16 May 2022 |newspaper=Wall Street Journal |via=www.wsj.com}}</ref> His father, Kermit Snyder, was an accountant and his mother, Phyllis Snyder, was an elementary school teacher. He attended [[Owen J. Roberts High School]] and later earned a BA in chemistry and biology from the [[University of Rochester]]. Snyder completed a PhD in biology from the [[California Institute of Technology]], where he trained in the laboratory of [[Norman Davidson (biologist)|Norman Davidson]].<ref name="auto10">{{Cite news |last=Sukel |first=Kayt |title=Making It Personal: Geneticist Michael Snyder Puts a Face on Personalized Medicine |url=https://psmag.com/social-justice/making-it-personal-geneticist-michael-snyder-puts-a-face-to-personalized-medicine-57554 |accessdate=16 May 2022 |website=Pacific Standard}}</ref><ref name=Beadle>{{cite web |url=https://genestogenomes.org/snyder-beadle/ |title=Congratulations to Michael Snyder for receiving the 2019 George W. Beadle Award! |last=Schmidt |first=Silke |date=9 April 2019 |website=Genetics Society of America |access-date=8 February 2021}}</ref> He pursued postdoctoral training at [[Stanford University School of Medicine|Stanford]] under [[Ronald W. Davis]].<ref name=Beadle/> 

== Career and appointments ==
Snyder began his academic career at [[Yale University]] in 1986 as an assistant professor in the department of biology.<ref name="auto10"/> He was granted tenure at Yale in 1994 and became chair of the new molecular, cellular, and developmental biology (MCDB) department from 1998 to 2004. During his tenure at Yale, he also directed the Center for Genomics and Proteomics.<ref name="auto5" /><ref name=Beadle/> His research at Yale included work on chromosome segregation and cell polarity, leading to the identification of a number of related genes.<ref>{{cite journal |vauthors=Page BD, Snyder M |title=CIK1: a developmentally regulated spindle pole body-associated protein important for microtubule functions in Saccharomyces cerevisiae |journal=Genes Dev |volume=6 |issue=8 |pages=1414–29 |date=August 1992 |pmid=1644287 |doi=10.1101/gad.6.8.1414 |s2cid=24949358 |url=|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name="auto8">{{cite journal |vauthors=Roemer T, Madden K, Chang J, Snyder M |title=Selection of axial growth sites in yeast requires Axl2p, a novel plasma membrane glycoprotein |journal=Genes Dev |volume=10 |issue=7 |pages=777–93 |date=April 1996 |pmid=8846915 |doi=10.1101/gad.10.7.777 |url=|doi-access=free }}</ref>

In 2009, Snyder joined [[Stanford University]], where he chaired the genetics department until 2024 and directs the Stanford Center for Genomics and Personalized Medicine.<ref name="auto7" /><ref name="Beadle" /> He has also served as [[principal investigator]] of the Center of Excellence in the Genome Sciences (CEGS) from 2001 to 2011 and was co-director of the CIRM Center for Stem Cell Genomics,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cirm.ca.gov/researchers/genomics-initiative/about|title=The CIRM Center of Excellence in Stem Cell Genomics (CESCG)|date=26 February 2015|website=California's Stem Cell Agency|accessdate=16 May 2022}}</ref> as well as director for the Center for Genome of Gene Regulation.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://med.stanford.edu/news/all-news/2015/02/snyder-awarded-7-million-from-genome-institute.html|title=Snyder awarded $7.1 million from genome institute|website=News Center|accessdate=16 May 2022}}</ref> 

Snyder was president of the US [[Human Proteome Organization]] from 2006 to 2008, elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2015, and president of the international [[Human Proteome Organization]] from 2017 to 2018.<ref name="auto3">{{Cite web |date=13 September 2023 |title=Michael Snyder |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/michael-snyder |website=American Academy of Arts and Sciences}}</ref> He led the [[National Institutes of Health]]'s Encyclopedia of DNA Elements ([[ENCODE]])'s production center for mapping regulatory regions of the human genome.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/9247694 | title=RePORT ⟩ RePORTER }}</ref>

Snyder has co-founded biotechnology companies, including Personalis,<ref name="auto9">{{Cite news |last=Eisenberg |first=Anne |date=2 June 2012 |title=A Geneticist's Research Turns Personal |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2012/06/03/business/geneticists-research-finds-his-own-diabetes.html |accessdate=16 May 2022 |newspaper=The New York Times}}</ref> SensOmics,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sensomics.com/|title=SensOmics, See the Unseen|website=SensOmics, See the Unseen}}</ref> Qbio,<ref name="auto">{{Cite news |last=Maxted |first=Anna |title=What's your ageing type? The four ways we grow old |date=21 January 2020 |url=https://www.thetimes.com/article/whats-your-ageing-type-the-four-ways-we-grow-old-bhd2lrscp |access-date=16 May 2022 |via=www.thetimes.co.uk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.q.bio/about |title=Our Mission and Values|website=www.q.bio|accessdate=16 May 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://stanfordmag.org/contents/body-count|title=Body Count|first=STANFORD|last=magazine|date=17 November 2021|website=stanfordmag.org|accessdate=16 May 2022}}</ref> January AI,<ref name="auto6">{{Cite news |last=Ravindran |first=Sandeep |date=14 March 2022 |title=Here Come the Artificial Intelligence Nutritionists |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/03/14/well/eat/ai-diet-personalized.html |accessdate=16 May 2022 |newspaper=The New York Times}}</ref> Filtricine, Mirvie, Protos, Protometrix<ref name="auto2">{{Cite web |date=2 April 2004 |title=Invitrogen Buys Protein Chip Maker Protometrix |url=https://www.genomeweb.com/archive/invitrogen-buys-protein-chip-maker-protometrix |accessdate=16 May 2022 |website=Genomeweb}}</ref> (now part of [[Thermo Fisher Scientific]]), Affomix<ref name="auto4">{{Cite web |title=Michael Snyder |url=https://online.stanford.edu/instructors/michael-snyder |website=online.stanford.edu}}</ref> (now part of [[Illumina, Inc.|Illumina]]),<ref>{{cite web |title=Snyder Lab |url=https://med.stanford.edu/snyderlab/about.html |website=Stanford.edu |access-date=2 December 2021}}</ref> and Iollo.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Weintraub |first=Karen |title=A geneticist studied one drop of his blood – and saw things he couldn't from a vial of blood |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/health/2023/01/19/stanford-michael-snyder-microsample-blood-health-insights/11076042002/ |access-date=2025-03-12 |website=USA TODAY |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Research==
Snyder has made contributions to medicine, genomics, and biotechnology. Snyder's laboratory has invented a number of novel systems-wide and genomics technologies, including RNA-Seq for mapping transcriptomes,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Wang |first1=Zhong |last2=Gerstein |first2=Mark |last3=Snyder |first3=Michael |date=January 2009 |title=RNA-Seq: a revolutionary tool for transcriptomics |journal=Nature Reviews Genetics |language=en |volume=10 |issue=1 |pages=57–63 |doi=10.1038/nrg2484 |issn=1471-0056 |pmc=2949280 |pmid=19015660}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Nagalakshmi |first1=Ugrappa |last2=Wang |first2=Zhong |last3=Waern |first3=Karl |last4=Shou |first4=Chong |last5=Raha |first5=Debasish |last6=Gerstein |first6=Mark |last7=Snyder |first7=Michael |date=2008-06-06 |title=The Transcriptional Landscape of the Yeast Genome Defined by RNA Sequencing |journal=Science |language=en |volume=320 |issue=5881 |pages=1344–1349 |doi=10.1126/science.1158441 |issn=0036-8075 |pmc=2951732 |pmid=18451266|bibcode=2008Sci...320.1344N }}</ref> NextGen Paired end sequencing for mapping genomes,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Korbel |first1=Jan O. |last2=Urban |first2=Alexander Eckehart |last3=Affourtit |first3=Jason P. |last4=Godwin |first4=Brian |last5=Grubert |first5=Fabian |last6=Simons |first6=Jan Fredrik |last7=Kim |first7=Philip M. |last8=Palejev |first8=Dean |last9=Carriero |first9=Nicholas J. |last10=Du |first10=Lei |last11=Taillon |first11=Bruce E. |last12=Chen |first12=Zhoutao |last13=Tanzer |first13=Andrea |last14=Saunders |first14=A. [[eukaryote]] [[model organism]] commonly used in genetics and molecular biology,<ref name="Bechard2021">{{cite news |last1=Bechard |first1=Deni Ellis |title=Body Count: How Michael Snyder's self-monitoring project could transform human health |url=https://stanfordmag.org/contents/body-count |access-date=2 December 2021 |work=Stanford Magazine |date=December 2021}}</ref> where he launched the large scale analysis of genes and proteins. Later, the lab began to use the same techniques to look at the human genome.<ref name="Bechard2021" /> His laboratory performed the first multi omics analysis of a human and pioneered the field of precision health.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mason |first=Christine Marie |title=Episode # 152: You As a Data Stream |url=https://rosewoman.com/blogs/rosewoman-podcast/episode-152-you-as-a-data-stream |access-date=10 August 2025 |website=The Rose Woman Podcast}}</ref>

In 2003, the [[ENCODE|Encyclopedia of DNA Elements]] (ENCODE) project was launched by the US [[National Human Genome Research Institute]] (NHGRI), with the goal of identifying all functional elements in the human genome. He has been a principal investigator in the ENCODE project since its inception in 2003 and the Snyder lab has contributed a large number of data sets.<ref name=Beadle />

== Awards==
In recognition for "developing and disseminating widely-used technology for the simultaneous analysis of thousands of genes, RNA molecules, and proteins" Snyder received the 2019 [[Genetics Society of America]] (GSA) [[George W. Beadle Award]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Congratulations to Michael Snyder for receiving the 2019 George W. Beadle Award! |url=https://genestogenomes.org/snyder-beadle/ |access-date=2025-03-12 |website=Genes to Genomes |language=en}}</ref> In 2025, Snyder was awarded the Precision Medicine World Conference Pioneer Award for his contributions to Precision Medicine.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Speaker Template |url=https://pmwcintl.com/speaker/michael-snyder-59_stanford_2025sv |access-date=2025-03-12 |website=PMWC Precision Medicine World Conference |language=en-US}}</ref>
